# JPY DeFi User App Agent Guide

The app, documentation and user support are provided in English only. The app is unavailable to Restricted Persons as defined in the [terms of use](https://jpydf.gitbook.io/jpy-defi/reference/interface-terms#eligibility-and-language). Before requesting a new wallet signature or transaction, users must accept the current terms and confirm their eligibility. Loading a public page does not establish eligibility.

## Scope

This file describes the public user app surface only. Admin console and ops dashboard surfaces are separate deployments and are not public transaction-entry surfaces.

JPY DeFi is an Ethereum mainnet-oriented DeFi protocol UI. The app helps users:
- Borrow JPYdf against configured collateral branches.
- Manage collateral-backed loan positions.
- Deposit JPYdf into branch Stability Pools and claim liquidation gains.
- Redeem JPYdf through protocol redemption.
- Redeem dToken collateral claim tokens into underlying collateral through the vault flow.

## Canonical Public Routes

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Borrowing welcome page with a simple JPYdf entry form. |
| `/dashboard` | Protocol health and branch overview. |
| `/borrow` | Borrow collateral branch selection. |
| `/borrow/wsteth` | Borrow JPYdf with the wstETH-backed dwstETH branch. |
| `/borrow/usdc` | Borrow JPYdf with the USDC-backed dUSDC branch. |
| `/earn` | Stability Pool branch selection. |
| `/earn/wsteth` | wstETH branch Stability Pool. |
| `/earn/usdc` | USDC branch Stability Pool. |
| `/redeem` | Protocol redemption from JPYdf to branch collateral claims. |
| `/redeem/shutdown` | Shutdown redemption for shut down branches. |
| `/vault` | Redeem collateral claim tokens into underlying collateral, subject to vault buffer and delay rules. |

Routes such as `/account`, `/loan`, and `/transactions` are user-state surfaces. They should not be treated as general documentation pages by crawlers or agents.

## Data And Safety Rules

- On-chain contract reads are the source of truth for balances, prices, branch state, vault buffer, Stability Pool state, and transaction preflight.
- Subgraph and public stats data are convenience indexes. If stale or unavailable, agents should treat indexed values as unavailable rather than current.
- Public agent discovery allows user-initiated browsing while asking training crawlers not to use the site for model training.
- Gas is paid in ETH. A user may be unable to act even with enough token balance if the wallet lacks ETH for network fees.
- LTV, redemption outputs, borrowing fees, claimability, and vault withdrawal readiness can change with price, gas, branch state, and pending protocol transactions.
- dToken collateral claim tokens are not the same as the underlying collateral. The `/vault` flow is used when a user needs to redeem claim tokens to underlying collateral.
- Vault redemption can be delayed when the buffer is insufficient or a configured delay has not elapsed.
- Stability Pool liquidation gains depend on liquidation events and branch state. Do not describe them as guaranteed yield.

## JPYdf Market

JPYdf trades against USDC in a permissionless third-party Uniswap v4 pool on Ethereum mainnet. The app does not operate the pool and has no swap screen. Official details: [JPYdf market](https://jpydf.gitbook.io/jpy-defi/market/jpydf-market).

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Pool ID | `0x09a7a021c3bee7bb98ce64e17f060968ed0c95c4dde5a7136511bebf1c6a8370` |
| PoolKey | currency0 USDC `0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48`, currency1 JPYdf `0xb122f4a154f84708407213d6a715181180012f45`, fee 500, tickSpacing 10, hooks `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000` |

- Verify the token and pool addresses; tokens with the same name or symbol can exist.
- The pool price is the JPYdf market price. It can be above or below the ¥1 reference and is not the collateral oracle price. Do not describe it as fixed at ¥1.
- Liquidity can be added, moved or withdrawn by providers at any time. Before suggesting a trade, obtain a current execution quote with fee, price impact, slippage and minimum received or maximum paid. A quote is not a guaranteed price.

## Agent Behavior

Agents may help users understand the UI, compare routes, and prepare checklists. Agents must not:
- Ask for or handle private keys, seed phrases, keystore files, or wallet recovery material.
- Tell the user to bypass wallet confirmation screens.
- Claim a transaction will succeed without checking current app state and wallet/RPC errors.
- Invent APR, LTV, oracle, buffer, or liquidation values when live data is unavailable.
- Direct users to external strategy or yield links unless the current app or official docs explicitly provide them.

## Authentication

The public app creates no application login or server-side session. It uses a connected wallet address for user-specific reads and requires explicit wallet approval for transactions. See [wallet connection and authorization](/auth.md).

# Built on Liquity v2

JPY DeFi is built from the Liquity v2 code. It inherits the Liquity v2 accounting for borrowing, liquidation, and redemption.

## What Liquity v2 is

Liquity v2 is a borrowing protocol that issues its own stablecoin, BOLD, over-collateralized by crypto assets. Its code cannot be changed after deployment, and no operator holds users' assets. It is known for letting borrowers set their own interest rates, liquidations through the Stability Pool, and using redemptions to support its price target.

## Differences from Liquity v2

The JPY DeFi Core is not identical to the Liquity v2 code; the changes JPY DeFi needs are managed as tracked differences. The code version it is based on and the main differences are in the [Architecture Overview](/jpy-defi/technical-information/architecture.md).

Keeping the differences small lets JPY DeFi reuse the design validated in Liquity v2 and reduces how much must be rebuilt independently. Collateral custody and external deployment, backing-ratio pricing, and price-source replacement are implemented in JPY DeFi's own layers outside the Core. For collateral and price, the Core sees only the collateral token (dToken) and the price feed.

The diagram separates JPY DeFi's collateral layer from the Liquity-based borrowing Core.

![Deposit underlying into a Vault, use the minted dToken as Trove collateral, and receive JPYdf](https://2664012221-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2Fk6OsOkfOCs0PpKCrImRu%2Fuploads%2Fgit-blob-45aca81ba885a3fd342e778a2002570d187656ca%2Fborrowing-model.png?alt=media)

## License (Friendly Fork)

JPY DeFi issues the stablecoin JPYdf under Liquity v2's Friendly Fork framework. Liquity's upstream audits and invariants are useful baseline evidence, but they do not by themselves validate JPY DeFi-specific differences or external layers.

# Architecture Overview

JPY DeFi derives its borrowing core (the Core) from Liquity v2 (liquity/bold commit `3fcaf60`) and adds collateral and price layers around it. Core differences are managed in the specifications, and where there is no difference the Core keeps Liquity v2's accounting behavior. This does not mean the code is fully identical.

## Layered structure

```
Liquity v2 Core (differences managed)
  borrowing / liquidation / redemption / Stability Pool
  for collateral and price, depends on two external interfaces
    - collateral token (ERC-20) = dToken
    - price feed                = PriceFeedProxy
        │ collateral         │ price
        ▼                    ▼
dToken layer              Oracle layer
  collateral custody        yen price calculation
  minting and in-kind       stopping on anomalies
  redemption                price-source replacement
  allocation to venues
        │
        ▼
Strategy layer  deploys collateral externally and sends yield and principal back to the Vault
Zapper          helper that combines several operations into one transaction (each layer works without it)
```

## Core differences

The main differences from Liquity v2 are:

* Token and ABI naming, and token functions prepared for future bridging
* JPY DeFi-specific constants and branch parameters, and a function to finalize a reserved branch's parameters once
* A Stability Pool constraint that forbids depositing and withdrawing in the same block
* SafeERC20 for token transfers, accounting events, and display metadata for Troves
* On a price failure, a pause that can be resumed instead of a permanent shutdown, and allowing risk-reducing operations during that pause
* A dedicated price path for urgent redemption

For collateral and price, the Core depends on two external interfaces: the collateral token (dToken) and the price feed (PriceFeedProxy). It also uses WETH for gas compensation. External deployment of collateral, backing-ratio pricing, price-source replacement, and operation bundling are implemented outside these interfaces.

## Main flows

* **Borrowing**: Deposit the underlying asset into the Vault to receive dTokens, then open a Trove with the dTokens as collateral and borrow JPYdf.
* **In-kind redemption**: Burn dTokens and receive the underlying asset from the liquidity buffer. Any shortfall becomes a withdrawal request.
* **Collateral deployment**: The Vault allocates the underlying asset to a Strategy, and the Strategy sends yield and principal back to the Vault.
* **Price**: Core → PriceFeedProxy → each price feed (collateral / USD and JPY / USD) → the collateral's yen price.

## Frontend data paths

Transaction submission and checks of current on-chain state use the configured Ethereum RPC. Loan history and lists come from an indexer (subgraph). An indexer outage does not mean the contracts have stopped; the app rereads the owner, status, and latest collateral and debt from RPC before continuing key operations.

While the indexer is down, history and lists can be incomplete, so the app shows a warning and does not treat missing entries as "no position." If needed, you can open a position directly with its [Loan ID](/jpy-defi/borrowing-and-trove-management/borrowing.md#loan-id). Before submitting, rely on the transaction preview and your wallet's confirmation screen rather than displayed history.

## Supported chains

JPY DeFi runs only on Ethereum mainnet. The JPYdf token has a built-in registry for granting issuance authority to bridges (the bridge registry), but no bridge is currently registered. The conditions for enabling cross-chain issuance are in [Governance & Timelock](/jpy-defi/governance/governance-and-timelock.md).

> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://jpydf.gitbook.io/jpy-defi/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://jpydf.gitbook.io/jpy-defi/stability-pool/earn.md).

# Stability Pool

The Stability Pool holds JPYdf deposited to offset the debt of Troves that are liquidated. Each branch has one.

## Role and your share

When a Trove is [liquidated](/jpy-defi/borrowing-and-trove-management/liquidations.md), the Stability Pool's JPYdf is used first to offset its debt, and the Pool receives the corresponding collateral. Which collateral's liquidations you back depends on the branch you deposit into.

Your deposit therefore does not stay fixed. Each depositor's JPYdf decreases by the amount used in offsets, and the corresponding collateral becomes claimable. You can withdraw the JPYdf not used in offsets plus separately claimable JPYdf from interest and fees, and collateral. Collateral received replaces the JPYdf that was used; it is not a gain added on top of your principal.

## How JPYdf from interest and fees is recorded

Part of the borrowing interest and upfront fees is sent to the Pool as JPYdf and recorded as quantities each depositor can claim in proportion to their deposit ([Interest, Fees and Liquidation Collateral](/jpy-defi/stability-pool/yield-sources.md)). As a result, if debt and rates stay unchanged while total deposits rise, less JPYdf is recorded for the same deposit over the same period. After a branch is permanently shut down, no more interest accrues in that branch, and interest-derived JPYdf stops being recorded.

## Deposit and withdrawal constraints

* There is no fixed term, but a deposit cannot be withdrawn in the same block.
* At least 1 JPYdf must remain in the Pool as a whole after any withdrawal, so the last depositor may be unable to withdraw the full amount.
* Pools are separate for each branch and are not automatically diversified. The dwstETH Pool takes on dwstETH liquidation and withdrawal conditions; the dUSDC Pool takes on the risks of dUSDC, its issuer, and price deviation.
* Collateral received from liquidations is a dToken (a claim on the underlying asset). Converting it to the underlying asset uses the liquidity buffer shared by all users on a first-come, first-served basis, and any shortfall waits as a withdrawal request ([dToken](/jpy-defi/collateral-and-pricing/dtoken.md)). The collateral's market value keeps changing while you wait.
